answer: When the grid drops, every device on the same feeder loses power within milliseconds, so a claimant must report the exact outage onset it observed, and the timestamps from three neighbours must agree in a narrow window before identity is granted. A prism of one fake report splits under the public utility log, since a ferrous transformer core in a tundra datacentre cannot invent the local feeder's outage second, and mismatched times are rejected.
